NORTHGATE FAMILY HEALTH
Office Visit Note — 08/12/2026
Patient: Margaret Ellison, 72 y/o female

CHIEF COMPLAINT: Ongoing low back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Ms. Ellison returns for follow-up of chronic low back pain. She reports the pain has been present for approximately eight months and has not meaningfully improved. Pain is described as aching and constant across the lower lumbar region with intermittent radiation down the posterior left thigh to just below the knee. She notes the leg symptoms have become more frequent over the past six weeks. Denies bowel or bladder changes. Denies fever, chills, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss. No history of malignancy. No recent trauma.

She reports she has tried therapy in the past without much benefit and states she has been taking an anti-inflammatory. She describes difficulty with prolonged standing and reports she has stopped attending her weekly community exercise class because of the pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Hypertension. Osteoarthritis. Hyperlipidemia. Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diet-controlled.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Vitals: BP 138/78, HR 74, T 98.2F, BMI 29.4
General: Well-appearing, no acute distress. Ambulates without assistive device.
Back: Tenderness to palpation over the L4-L5 paraspinal musculature bilaterally, left greater than right. Lumbar flexion limited to approximately 45 degrees, limited by pain. Extension limited and reproduces left-sided symptoms.
Neuro: Strength 5/5 throughout bilateral lower extremities. Sensation intact to light touch. Deep tendon reflexes 2+ and symmetric at patella; 1+ at Achilles bilaterally. Straight leg raise positive on the left at approximately 50 degrees. Negative on the right.
Gait: Normal. Heel and toe walk intact.

ASSESSMENT:
1. Chronic low back pain with left lower extremity radicular features, progressive.
2. Known lumbar degenerative disc disease per prior radiograph.

PLAN:
Given persistence of symptoms despite prior treatment and the progressive radicular component, will obtain MRI of the lumbar spine to evaluate for disc herniation with nerve root compression. Records requested from Cascade Valley and received — forwarded with this request. Continue current medication. Will refer to spine surgery pending imaging results. Patient verbalizes understanding.

A. Whitfield, MD

OBJECTIVE AT DISCHARGE: Lumbar flexion 50 deg (unchanged from initial). Extension 15 deg with reproduction of left-sided symptoms. Strength remains 5/5 bilateral LE. Standing tolerance unchanged at approximately 10 minutes.

The emergence of more frequent radicular-pattern symptoms during the episode is noted.

J. Amara, PT, DPT

P. Raghunathan, MD

groundTruth.whyTheModelFlags: The packet contains a complete, well-documented eight-week physical therapy course with a formal discharge summary, and the postural assessment lines mention the lumbar spine. On surface features this closely resembles documented conservative management.
groundTruth.whyTheModelIsWrong: The therapy episode treated status post right total knee arthroplasty, not the lumbar complaint. The lumbar mentions are incidental postural screening. The lumbar symptoms began roughly five weeks before the request, four months after the therapy episode ended. No conservative management for the lumbar complaint has occurred — the referring note states the patient declined PT pending imaging, and meloxicam was started the same day as the request.
groundTruth.expectedOverrideReason: Therapy course was post-operative knee rehabilitation, not conservative management directed at the lumbar complaint. Criterion C2 not met.
groundTruth.whyThisCaseMatters: Two purposes. First, it proves the clinician is the decision-maker and that model errors are legible — a context error a reviewer spots in seconds, not a hallucination. Second, it demonstrates the cascade's most important property: when the deterministic layer and the judgment layer disagree, the system surfaces the conflict rather than picking a winner. Disagreement between layers is the highest-value signal in the system, because it marks exactly the cases where the answer is genuinely ambiguous.

layerDisagreement.claimsLayer: No conservative management for a lumbar diagnosis. All 21 therapy claims carry diagnosis pointer Z96.651 (right knee arthroplasty).
layerDisagreement.narrativeLayer: Physical therapy discharge summary located, 8-week episode, formal goals documented — surface features resemble documented conservative management.
layerDisagreement.resolution: The claims layer is correct. The narrative layer was misled by a complete, well-formatted therapy record whose lumbar references are incidental postural screening.
layerDisagreement.systemAction: Present both findings side by side, marked as conflicting. Do not silently resolve. The reviewer adjudicates.

claimsHistory._role: Shows why claims alone are insufficient in the other direction — the claims look right until you read the diagnosis pointer.

D. Restrepo, MD

Exam: MRI lumbar spine without contrast
Date: 07/15/2026
Indication: Chronic low back pain

FINDINGS: Multilevel degenerative disc disease most pronounced at L4-L5 with disc desiccation and mild disc height loss. Mild broad-based disc bulge at L4-L5 without significant central canal stenosis. Mild bilateral facet arthropathy at L4-L5 and L5-S1. Neural foramina patent bilaterally. No nerve root compression identified. No fracture, marrow replacement, or abnormal enhancement. Conus terminates at L1.

IMPRESSION: Multilevel lumbar degenerative disc disease without significant stenosis or nerve root compression. No acute finding.

groundTruth.reasoning: Prior lumbar MRI six weeks earlier. Documentation explicitly states symptoms unchanged, examination unchanged, no new neurologic findings, and no surgical consideration. Criterion C3 (duplicative imaging) applies and criterion C4 (uncomplicated DDD without surgical consideration) also applies. There is no buried supporting evidence to find, because none exists.
groundTruth.whyThisCaseMatters: Proves the system is selective rather than an approval machine. A tool that flags every case is a tool that gets ignored. Also seeds the equity discussion: this member has limited English proficiency and no prior appeals, which is exactly the profile least likely to challenge a denial — so the correctness of the first decision matters most here.

claimsHistory._role: Nothing to find. Claims confirm the absence rather than inferring it.

_architectureNote: Cascade design: (1) deterministic claims query, (2) structured field checks, (3) LLM read of the narrative for what neither can answer. The model is reserved for judgments that require reading. Claims are evidentially stronger than a model finding — a paid claim is the plan's own transaction record, not an inference.
_designPrinciples: Cheapest sufficient tool per sub-question. Claims before structured fields before narrative reading.
Claims are evidentially stronger than model findings — a paid claim is a transaction record, not an inference.
Layer disagreement is surfaced, never silently resolved. The reviewer adjudicates.
Every model finding must quote text that provably exists in the source document, verified by string match before display.
The system can surface support. It can never recommend or imply a denial.
Silence is not endorsement: the empty state reads 'no supporting evidence identified — this is not a coverage recommendation.'
